question: What is the primary definition of an infection reservoir?

options.A: The natural habitat where a pathogen lives and multiplies
options.B: The specific medical tool used to administer vaccines
options.C: An immune human who cannot catch infectious diseases
options.D: Any inanimate object contaminated with hospital germs

explanation: Pathogens require a permanent home where they can thrive and reproduce before moving to a new host, which defines the reservoir. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T94#GNS214_U1_T94_h1)

question: Why is targeting the infection reservoir considered effective in public health?

options.A: It completely eliminates all bacteria from the human body
options.B: It stops the chain of transmission at its source
options.C: It guarantees that patients never need antibiotics
options.D: It lowers the financial cost of hospital building materials

explanation: Controlling the reservoir prevents the pathogen from existing in the environment, stopping the spread before it reaches vulnerable people. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T94#GNS214_U1_T94_h1)

question: Lassa fever spreading from rodents to humans represents which type of reservoir?
explanation: Animals that naturally carry diseases transmissible to humans are classified as animal reservoirs or zoonotic sources. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T94#GNS214_U1_T94_h2)

question: What makes human carriers dangerous as infection reservoirs?

options.A: They destroy the laboratory testing equipment
options.B: They are completely immune to all known drugs
options.C: They show no symptoms while spreading the disease
options.D: They always require immediate surgical intervention

explanation: Asymptomatic carriers do not feel sick, so they continue normal daily activities while unknowingly transmitting pathogens to others. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T94#GNS214_U1_T94_h2)

question: What is the main goal of active case finding in a community?

options.A: To collect data for hospital financial reports
options.B: To identify and treat infected people early
options.C: To build new primary health care clinics
options.D: To distribute free mosquito nets to children

explanation: Active screening helps discover hidden cases so treatment can start before the disease spreads further. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T94#GNS214_U1_T94_h3)

question: A patient completes a full course of prescribed antibiotics for a bacterial infection. What happens to their status as a reservoir?

options.A: They automatically develop resistance to all drugs
options.B: They stop being a source of infection for others
options.C: They permanently lose all natural immunity
options.D: They become an environmental reservoir instead

explanation: Successful treatment eradicates the pathogen from the patient, removing them as an active reservoir in the transmission chain. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T94#GNS214_U1_T94_h3)

question: Mass immunization of domestic dogs primarily helps prevent which disease in humans?
explanation: Dogs are the primary animal reservoir for rabies, and vaccinating them stops the virus from spreading to people through bites. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T94#GNS214_U1_T94_h4)

question: A rural health clinic notices an increase in Lassa fever cases linked to grain storage in homes. What is the best community intervention?

options.A: Teach villagers proper rodent-proof grain storage methods
options.B: Prescribe malaria tablets to every person in the village
options.C: Close the primary health clinic until the dry season
options.D: Advise everyone to stop eating local grains immediately

explanation: Securing food supplies keeps rodents away from human living spaces, cutting off the animal reservoir vector interaction. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T94#GNS214_U1_T94_h4)

question: Which chemical is most commonly used for disinfecting water and environmental surfaces during a cholera outbreak?
explanation: Chlorine compounds are effective at killing waterborne pathogens and decontaminating surfaces in outbreak settings. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T94#GNS214_U1_T94_h5)

question: Why is draining stagnant water around houses important for infection control?

options.A: It removes breeding grounds for disease vectors
options.B: It reduces the humidity inside residential buildings
options.C: It prevents the growth of beneficial house plants
options.D: It increases the mineral content of the soil

explanation: Stagnant water attracts insects and microorganisms that serve as vectors or reservoirs for infectious diseases. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T94#GNS214_U1_T94_h5)

question: What is the main difference between isolation and quarantine?

options.A: Isolation is for animals, while quarantine is strictly for human beings
options.B: Isolation separates sick people, while quarantine restricts exposed healthy people
options.C: Quarantine lasts for years, while isolation lasts for only one hour
options.D: Quarantine uses medications, while isolation only uses surgical masks

explanation: Isolation deals with confirmed infectious patients, whereas quarantine monitors individuals who had contact with an infection but show no symptoms yet. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T94#GNS214_U1_T94_h6)

question: A nurse cares for a patient with an active, highly contagious airborne infection. What is the correct nursing action regarding placement?

options.A: Allow family members to visit without restrictions
options.B: Transfer the patient to the general open ward
options.C: Place the patient in an isolation room
options.D: Send the patient home on quarantine status

explanation: Patients with active, contagious infections require isolation to protect other patients and staff in the healthcare facility. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T94#GNS214_U1_T94_h6)

question: What is the primary role of nurses in primary health care regarding infection reservoirs?

options.A: Enforcing strict police laws against market traders
options.B: Educating the community on hygiene and prevention
options.C: Manufacturing vaccines in large pharmaceutical plants
options.D: Building modern water treatment dams in cities

explanation: Nurses act as educators, teaching people simple lifestyle practices that eliminate environmental and domestic reservoirs. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T94#GNS214_U1_T94_h7)

question: A nurse notices villagers leaving drinking water uncovered in open clay pots. What is the best initial nursing response?

options.A: Confiscate all clay pots from the village market square
options.B: Report the village leaders to the federal ministry of health
options.C: Demonstrate how to cover the pots and explain why it stops contamination
options.D: Wait until an outbreak occurs before taking any action

explanation: Practical education empowers community members to protect their own water supply from environmental pathogens. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T94#GNS214_U1_T94_h7)
